name: BCI Recording Transcript Session 4471 Patient Anonymous
author: Meridian Neural Health Clinic, Tier 3
description:
BCI RECORDING TRANSCRIPT — SESSION 4471
PATIENT: [REDACTED]
CLINICIAN: Dr. Amira Johansson-Osei
SESSION TYPE: Neural-assisted trauma processing

[Note: BCI recordings capture the patient's neural-emotional state alongside verbal content. Emotional markers are indicated in brackets.]

DR. JOHANSSON-OSEI: When you're ready, tell me about the moment.

PATIENT: [anxiety spike, 7.2] It was during the upgrade. The tech — the Gray Zone tech, not a real surgeon — said I'd feel 'a little pressure.' [anger, 4.1] That's what they all say. 'A little pressure.'

DR. JOHANSSON-OSEI: What did you actually feel?

PATIENT: [anxiety spike, 8.9; fear, 6.3] I felt my old interface disconnect. There's a moment — maybe half a second — where you're between systems. The old one is offline and the new one hasn't initialized. You're neurologically naked. No augmented perception, no data overlay, no threat detection, no emotional buffering. Just your raw brain for the first time in years. [pause; grief, 7.8] I didn't recognize my own thoughts. They were so slow. So quiet. I thought something was wrong — I thought the tech had damaged me. But that was just... me. The unaugmented me. Thinking at biological speed.

DR. JOHANSSON-OSEI: And that frightened you.

PATIENT: [grief, 9.1; shame, 5.4] It terrified me. Not because it was bad. Because I realized I couldn't live like that anymore. I've been augmented since I was nineteen. I'm forty-three. I don't know who I am without the interface. I don't know if there's a person under all the hardware or just... a platform. Something the augmentation runs on.

[Session continues for 47 minutes. Full transcript available upon authorization.]

CLINICIAN NOTE: Patient exhibits classic interface dependency — the cognitive and emotional reliance on augmentation that develops after prolonged use. The moment of disconnection during upgrade triggered an identity crisis that the patient is still processing three months later. Recommend continued BCI-assisted therapy, with the ironic awareness that we are using the technology to treat the trauma caused by the technology.
story_hooks: Interface dependency — who are you without your augmentation?
The half-second of neurological nakedness during an upgrade
